executive_brief: The Football Match Manager is a structured data model designed to orchestrate the lifecycle of football matches, team management, and user tracking. It implements a relational pattern managing entities from Leagues down to User-Match follow relationships, ensuring strict data integrity through state-dependent validation rules for match statuses and scoring.

architectural_constraints: Match dateTime must be in future when status is 'upcoming'
homeScore and awayScore must be non-null and >= 0 when status is 'finished'
Team name must be globally unique
UserFollow must satisfy a composite unique constraint on (userId, matchId)
Team foundedYear range: 1800 to current year
String length limits: Venue max 200, Team name max 100, Team abbreviation max 5, Display name max 50
Match status restricted to Enum: upcoming, live, finished, postponed, cancelled

maturity_assessment: The specification provides a high-fidelity data schema with exhaustive validation rules, yet it remains in REFINEMENT status. While the technical completeness score is high, critical structural gaps exist: the lack of defined high-level Goals & Objectives and a clear Scope boundary creates ambiguity regarding the system's business purpose and the exclusion of player/referee statistics.
critical_dependencies: Foreign key dependency: Match depends on League (leagueId) and Team (homeTeamId, awayTeamId)
Foreign key dependency: UserFollow depends on User (userId) and Match (matchId)
Performance Index requirement: Match (leagueId, dateTime) and (status)
